original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: One proposition of PR4100: NORMAL-FORM.md's good-packet conjugation identity Q N(P) Q^-1=[[I-E,T],[J,I-JT]] over Z/q^w, its intermediate equalities, and its stated agreement with the retained controlled_normalizer.py coefficients and executed weighted address map.
scope_change_reason: The card prioritizes CRT.md total repair and COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift, which open PRs already audit. NORMAL-FORM.md is the BIT good-branch premise in PR4100's AUDIT table and had no independent check. Its quantified statement is an all-ring algebraic identity, so it is checked by a written re-derivation plus an exhaustive small-ring certificate, not substituted by a smoke test.
bottleneck_link: Side result for PR4100 acceptance: it settles one premise of the BIT good branch (AUDIT.md row 'Local-ring split ranks'). It changes no supplier, exponent or selected record.
stop_rule: Stop at the first failed written equality or vendor disagreement and report it; otherwise stop after the bounded domains below.
evidence: verify.py: 2,162 rank-r idempotents (1<=r<m) in seven exhaustive (ring, m) domains, with the census matched to the closed form |GL_m|/(|GL_r||GL_(m-r)|); 1,332 good packets among them; 1,763 good packets among 4,080 sampled chart projectors up to m=5; 3,509 good instances checked in total, including vendor-comparison charts; 2,177 vendor agreements on cross and the executed weighted map; both mutation controls rejected.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does the Schwartz-Zippel bad-packet bound 2*64^3/q in BIT.md hold per request for the actual header distribution, rather than for uniformly random low classes?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The recurrence charges bad packets at rate eta=1e-16; a worst-case header stream could make every request bad.
open_questions.first_step: Identify in BIT.md how request headers are generated and whether the bad fraction is a count over a complete packet enumeration or a probability.

open_questions.question: Is FALLBACK.md's 49,911-child bound sharp for the retained paid_children rule?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Opposite-orientation swaps cost one child, not three; a sharper count tightens F but cannot change kappa materially at eta=1e-16.
open_questions.first_step: Count same- and opposite-orientation swaps in compile_program for m=64 at the worst pivot itinerary.
